_comment: 2026 Senate cycle configuration for the control simulation. dem_safe_seats / rep_safe_seats count seats NOT in the competitive list (holdovers + safe 2026 races such as FL, NE, MT): of the 9 competitive races Democrats hold GA, MI, NH (3) and Republicans hold NC, ME, OH, TX, IA, AK (6), so dem_safe = 47-3 = 44 and rep_safe = 53-6 = 47. dem_majority_threshold is 51 because the sitting VP (R) breaks 50-50 ties. Fundamentals: each race carries the state's Dem-minus-Rep presidential margin in 2024 and 2020; the fundamentals prior blends them (pres_weight_recent on 2024) and is blended into the polling margin with weight blend_k/(blend_k+num_polls), so it anchors thinly-polled races and fades as polls accumulate. Candidate names are the general-election nominees (MI: El-Sayed won the Aug 4 primary; NH: Sununu is the Republican nominee) - the export falls back to each party's top-polled name when a configured name is missing from the polls. wikipedia overrides the default article title (Ohio is a special election). Each race's features block carries the incumbency and candidate-experience inputs to the fundamentals prior; statewide_wins for an incumbent exclude wins for this seat (those are the incumbency term).

fundamentals._comment: Fundamentals prior, Dem-minus-Rep points, written to be explained in plain language: prior = lean + national swing + incumbency + incumbent tenure + candidate office years + candidate statewide record + economy. LEAN starts from the state's 2024 presidential margin at full weight (pres_2024_weight 1.0) and moves it part-way toward how 2020 differed (pres_2020_shift_weight) and how the state's last Senate race differed (last_senate_shift_weight): lean = pres_2024 + w20*(pres_2020 - pres_2024) + wlast*(last_senate - pres_2024). SWING comes from national_environment (generic ballot + approval). INCUMBENCY is binary: +/-incumbency_advantage for the incumbent's party, times appointed_incumbent_factor if appointed. INCUMBENT TENURE is categorical on years in this seat (incumbent_tenure_schedule, toward the incumbent). CANDIDATE OFFICE YEARS is categorical on years in any elected office (office_years_schedule, for non-incumbent candidates; net D minus R). STATEWIDE RECORD is prior statewide general-election wins/losses (experience_per_statewide_win/_loss, capped). ECONOMY is in the economy block. Every value is exported per race. All coefficients are hand-set (see candidate_quality.py for the original vote-share versions) and swept in scripts/sensitivity_sweep.py.

incumbent_tenure_schedule._comment: years in this Senate seat -> extra pts toward the incumbent

office_years_schedule._comment: years in any elected office, non-incumbent candidates -> pts toward that candidate's party

fundamentals._midterm_comment: President's-party midterm penalty in margin points. 0 because the generic ballot already measures this cycle's climate; exposed so it can be switched on for a fundamentals-only view.

forecast._comment: calibration_bias_weight scales the historically-fitted poll bias (~-2.5) before it is applied: 0 = ignore it (fundamentals already capture the red-state lean), 1 = apply in full, 0.5 = split the difference. Kept at 0.5 to avoid double-counting the same Dem-overstatement that the fundamentals blend also corrects. bias_cycle_type selects which calibration cycles the bias is averaged over: 'all' (pooled 2018-2024, -2.5, dominated by the 2020 presidential-year miss) or 'midterm' (2018+2022 only, -0.4). Polling error does not carry a predictable sign from cycle to cycle, and the two midterms in the calibration set show ~zero bias, so a midterm forecast uses the midterm-only figure.
forecast._drift_comment: Extra national-error SD for campaign movement between today and election day: sigma_drift = campaign_drift_per_sqrt_day * sqrt(days_to_election), added in quadrature to the national sigma. 0.35/sqrt(day) gives ~1.9 pts a month out, ~1 pt a week out, and 0 on election day; polling averages have historically moved 2-3 pts over a final month. This is the only forward-looking term - the model is otherwise a nowcast.
forecast._tail_comment: Student-t degrees of freedom for polling error (variance-matched to the calibrated sigmas; null = Gaussian). Backtest on the 98 calibration races: t(5) Brier 0.0591 / log-loss 0.1905 vs Gaussian 0.0602 / 0.1952 — fat tails score better on both, and t(5) is the standard middle in the literature. Recomputed monthly in forecast_calibration.json under tail_comparison.
forecast._market_comment: Weight on prediction-market odds in each race's blend. 0 = polls + fundamentals only (the published forecast); market prices are still fetched and shown for comparison.

national_environment._comment: The midterm climate, applied as a uniform swing on top of each state's presidential lean (so the fundamentals prior reflects today, not 2024). Expected national Dem-minus-Rep margin = generic_weight*generic_ballot + approval_weight*(approval-implied margin for the out-party); the swing is that minus the 2024 House baseline. president_party is the in-party that pays the midterm penalty. approval_to_margin_coef converts the president's net approval to their party's national margin. senate_responsiveness scales how much of the national swing reaches Senate races. It only moves the fundamentals prior — polled races already price the climate in, so this mainly lifts thinly-polled seats.

polls._comment: House-effect correction from our own pollster-grade analysis (config/forecast_calibration.json: mean actual-minus-poll error per pollster over 2018-2024 Senate races, n>=5 polls). A pollster's relative house effect = its mean error minus the pooled mean (so the cycle-wide miss is not double-counted), shrunk by n/(n+shrink_k) and capped at +/-cap, then ADDED to each of its polls' Dem-minus-Rep margin before the race average. Pollsters with no historical record are left unadjusted; the share of a race's polls that were adjusted is exported. Pollster-quality grades (Silver Bulletin PPM) weight the polls separately in the averaging engine.

correlation._comment: Similarity-structured race error (Silver-style): similarity_share of the race-level variance is shared between states that vote alike, K_ij = region_weight*same_region + (1-region_weight)*exp(-|pres_2024_i - pres_2024_j|/lean_scale). Per-race variance is unchanged; the implied race-by-race correlation matrix is exported (error_correlation).

economy._comment: Economic fundamentals (data/fallback/economic.csv via src/data/economic.py), signed against the president's party. inflation: (CPI year-over-year % - inflation_baseline) * inflation_coef, national, applied to every race (kept small because approval already reflects it). gas: (state gas price - national) * gas_deviation_coef, per state. unemployment: (state rate - national) * unemployment_deviation_coef, per state. A missing series contributes 0 and is reported as unavailable.
